name: STACK Infrastructure
founded: January 2019 (Denver; launched by IPI Partners combining Infomart Data Centers' Ashburn, Portland and Silicon Valley facilities with IPI's Atlanta, Chicago and two Dallas/Fort Worth assets — 100MW+ across ~1.5M sq ft at launch)
ownership: private (Blue Owl Capital-managed digital infrastructure funds — formerly IPI Partners, the ICONIQ Capital/Iron Point Partners joint venture that created STACK; Blue Owl acquired IPI's business for ~$1.0B, completed January 2025; 11 stabilized US assets recycled into Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Trust, a perpetual-life non-traded REIT, December 2025)
employees: ~900 globally across ~20 markets (February 2025, per Blue Owl SEC filing — latest disclosed)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: STACK Infrastructure is the Blue Owl-managed wholesale developer-landlord executing two of the largest named-tenant data-center programs in the United States — developer and owner of all three campuses in Amazon's $18B northwest Louisiana buildout (raised from $12B on 18 August 2026) and of Project Jupiter, the 1GW+ Stargate campus in Santa Teresa, New Mexico serving Oracle/OpenAI — on a platform the company states at 13GW of current and pipeline capacity across three regionally financed businesses (December 2025). Ownership is in motion at both ends of the structure: Blue Owl acquired STACK's fund manager IPI Partners (~$1.0B, closed January 2025), carved the pan-European colocation business out to Apollo funds (April 2025), seeded a perpetual non-traded REIT with 11 stabilized STACK data centers at $3.3B gross value (December 2025), and — per Bloomberg-sourced reporting, June 2026 — is preparing a sale of the APAC portfolio that could exceed $30B. BACKGROUND: Denver-headquartered; formed January 2019 when IPI Partners (the ICONIQ Capital/Iron Point Partners JV) combined Infomart Data Centers with T5-operated assets — 100MW+ across six US markets at launch under founding CEO Brian Cox (ex-Infomart CEO, ex-Cologix CFO/COO). Today more than 90 US data centers in operation, under construction and under development (company statement, August 2026); Americas site capacity 3,200MW across 23 campuses — 2,400MW of it in Northern Virginia — plus EMEA at 743MW across 21 campuses post-carve-out and APAC campuses in Melbourne, Sydney, Tokyo, Osaka and Johor Bahru. Regional chief executives: Matt VanderZanden (Americas, since December 2025), Brian Cox (EMEA interim, since August 2025), Preet Gona (APAC). Repeat securitizer: ten ABS series under its master trust since 2019 (~$3.9B cumulative issuance), within $36.1B of global capital raised as of July 2025. No revenue or EBITDA figures are disclosed.
ecosystemRole: We assess STACK as the Blue Owl complex's build engine and, alongside Vantage, one of the two most consequential private wholesale landlords in the current hyperscaler/Stargate buildout. Basis: company and partner releases — named developer-owner roles for Amazon (three Louisiana campuses, $18B) and for Oracle/OpenAI's Stargate program (Project Jupiter, one of five sites in the 4.5GW expansion), one of the sector's longest-running data-center securitization programs (ten series since 2019), and a three-region platform that its sponsor actively recycles (Apollo colocation carve-out, perpetual-REIT seeding, reported APAC sale process). For power-chain and construction vendors, STACK is a standardized procurement counterparty: a repeatable design — closed-loop cooling with potable-water use held to office-building levels, on-site substations, liquid-to-chip readiness — replicated across more than 90 US facilities and three continents.

productsAndServices.name: Americas hyperscale platform (core business)
productsAndServices.description: Build-own-operate wholesale campuses and build-to-suit programs across 23 Americas campuses totaling 3,200MW of site capacity on 1,360 acres (company site, August 2026). Northern Virginia is the anchor — 7 sites and 2,400MW, led by the Stafford Technology Campus (1+GW across ~500 acres, 19 data centers in four sub-campuses, Dominion Energy substations), the 200MW/62-acre NVA05 campus in Manassas ($900M green financing, January 2025) and a 144MW two-building Loudoun County campus (announced February 2025). Beyond Virginia: DFW02 in Lancaster, south Dallas (220MW initial across six 36MW buildings, expandable past 500MW, on-site Oncor substation), Phoenix (2 sites, 500MW), Portland (3 sites, 250MW), Silicon Valley (2 sites, 200MW), Atlanta (2 sites, 180MW), Chicago (2 sites, 76MW — CHI02, a 36MW two-story facility in Elk Grove Village, added March 2025), New Albany OH (60MW), Toronto (56MW) and Calgary. Two named-tenant mega-programs now dominate the pipeline: three campuses for Amazon across Caddo Parish, Bossier Parish and Shreveport, Louisiana ($18B program), and Project Jupiter, a 1GW+ Stargate campus in Santa Teresa, New Mexico developed with BorderPlex Digital Assets for Oracle/OpenAI.
highlights: Developer and owner of all three campuses in Amazon's $18B northwest Louisiana program — up to 750 full-time and ~2,250 construction jobs (Amazon, August 2026)
Project Jupiter is one of five sites in Oracle/OpenAI's 4.5GW Stargate expansion — construction began September 2025, initial operations targeted Q4 2026
Company claims the position of largest private data center developer in Virginia, with $9B of Virginia financings since 2019 (March 2025 release)
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the small set of private wholesale platforms delivering gigawatt-class named-tenant campuses — bigger US program wins than Aligned or QTS's disclosed AI deals, and a peer of Vantage in Stargate delivery, though at smaller total platform scale (13GW current + pipeline vs Vantage's ~9GW power capacity claim); unlike Equinix/Digital Realty it carries no public-REIT overhead and prices delivery credibility, not interconnection ecosystems.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term take-or-pay wholesale leases, build-to-suit development agreements and powered-shell leases direct with hyperscalers; project debt raised against leases via green loans and the master-trust ABS program.
targetSegments: Enterprises on legacy sites (Plano since 2012, Silicon Valley, Portland)
productsAndServices.roadmap: DFW02 first phase delivery from mid-2026; Project Jupiter initial operations Q4 2026; Louisiana three-campus buildout ramping to ~2,250 construction jobs; Stafford's 19-building program phased over multiple years.

productsAndServices.name: Deployment tiers: powered shell, turnkey wholesale, build-to-suit
productsAndServices.description: STACK launched in 2019 selling an explicit product ladder — HYPER STACK (hyperscale campuses and build-to-suit), READY STACK (turnkey wholesale colocation) and POWER STACK (powered shell) — and still sells all three rungs, now framed as campus development, single-tenant purpose-built facilities and multi-tenant data halls. Powered shell delivers the building plus utility power with the tenant self-performing electrical/mechanical fit-out; turnkey delivers the complete environment. Campuses are engineered to accommodate both in one footprint (DFW02 explicitly supports shell and turnkey deployments), with cloud-density and AI/ML-density configurations and liquid-to-chip cooling options for high-density work.
highlights: Land-and-power banking is the underlying asset: on-site substations at DFW02 (Oncor), NVA05 (NOVEC) and Stafford (Dominion) convert utility position into deliverable megawatts
First-megawatt speed plus long-term scalability is the stated campus design goal
Closed-loop cooling standard: zero potable water for cooling on new US designs, water use held to office-building levels at Project Jupiter
productsAndServices.positioning: The retained shell-through-turnkey flexibility differentiates against turnkey-only wholesale peers (Vantage, CloudHQ) and appeals to hyperscalers that self-perform fit-out; against powered-shell specialists, STACK's operating track record (>90 US facilities) supports the full-service rung.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Wholesale leases per tier — powered-shell leases, turnkey data-hall leases, and build-to-suit development agreements; no retail colocation or interconnection product remains after the 2025 Apollo carve-out of the European colo business.
targetSegments: Large enterprises taking single data halls
productsAndServices.roadmap: AI/ML-density configurations rolling into new campuses (DFW02, Jupiter, Louisiana); no dated public roadmap for tier-level product changes.

productsAndServices.name: EMEA hyperscale platform (post-carve-out)
productsAndServices.description: 743MW across 21 campuses on 322 acres (company site, August 2026): Milan is the largest market (11 sites, 399MW — the Supernap Italia legacy plus >100,000 sqm of expansion land in Siziano), followed by Frankfurt (96MW — market entry via an 80MW hyperscale campus in Liederbach), Zurich (3 sites, 76MW), Copenhagen (72MW), Geneva (3 sites, 42MW), Oslo (2 sites, 40MW) and Stockholm (18MW). The platform was assembled by acquisition — Supernap Italia (February 2021) and Nordic operator DigiPlex (August 2021) — and launched as STACK EMEA in February 2022 with 16 markets and 400MW+ under development. In April 2025 Apollo-managed funds agreed to acquire the pan-European colocation business (seven data centers across Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen, Milan and Geneva, serving carriers, IT firms and financial institutions), which is being rebranded away from the STACK name under CEO Sherif Rizkalla — leaving STACK EMEA focused on hyperscale wholesale under interim CEO Brian Cox (since August 2025).
highlights: Colo carve-out to Apollo (April 2025) is a deliberate pruning to hyperscale-only in Europe
Milan's 399MW across 11 sites makes Italy the platform's European center of gravity
Nordic sites carry the DigiPlex 100%-renewable-power legacy
productsAndServices.positioning: Sub-scale against Vantage EMEA (15 campuses incl. 148MW CWL1) and the FLAP incumbents; the hyperscale-only refocus positions EMEA as a build-to-suit partner in Milan/Frankfurt rather than an interconnection or retail player.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Wholesale leases to hyperscale and cloud clients; the divested colo/interconnection business no longer sells under the STACK brand.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers and cloud majors in Milan and Frankfurt
AI/HPC tenants on Nordic renewable power
productsAndServices.roadmap: Frankfurt 80MW Liederbach campus buildout; Siziano land bank supports 80MW+ of additional Milan power; leadership transition beyond interim CEO unresolved.

productsAndServices.name: APAC platform (reported sale process)
productsAndServices.description: Five markets built since 2022 by partnership and JV entry: Melbourne (2 sites, 432MW — MEL01 in Truganina delivered STACK's first APAC data center in August 2023 and drew an AUD $1.3B green financing in July 2025), Sydney (SYD01 in Erskine Park — a 450MW campus filing made April 2025: three-story, ~82,000 sqm, 156 generators), Tokyo (TKY01 in Inzai, 36MW — ¥39.7B green financing October 2025; first 18MW building delivering 2026, 18MW more in 2027), Osaka (KIX01, 72MW, an ESR joint venture — first 18MW building RFS Q2 2027, LEED Gold pre-certified) and Johor Bahru (JHB01, 216MW on 10.8 hectares — first 120MW building phase 1 delivering from Q4 2026). Australia entry came via a June 2022 partnership with builder Hickory (124MW initial pipeline); Japan via the ESR JV. Per Bloomberg-sourced reporting (June 2026), Blue Owl is preparing a sale of the APAC portfolio that could exceed $30B, with the BlackRock/Microsoft/MGX-backed AI Infrastructure Partnership, Brookfield, IFM, KKR and DigitalBridge among reported suitors.
highlights: More than $2B of Australian financings executed since Q2 2024 (company, July 2025)
Johor's JHB01 sits in the Johor-Singapore corridor contested by Vantage, AirTrunk and ST Telemedia
A $30B+ APAC exit would be among the largest data-center transactions ever (reported, unconfirmed by the company)
productsAndServices.positioning: A younger, smaller APAC platform than AirTrunk or Vantage APAC, differentiated by market picks (Johor, Inzai, Kansai) and local-currency green financing; the reported sale would convert five years of platform building into a sponsor-level exit.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Wholesale leases; JV structures with ESR (Japan); local-currency project debt (AUD, JPY) from regional bank syndicates.
targetSegments: Cloud and AI providers in Tokyo/Osaka, Melbourne and Sydney
productsAndServices.roadmap: JHB01 phase 1 from Q4 2026; TKY01 18MW in 2026 + 18MW in 2027; KIX01A Q2 2027; SYD01 pending approvals; reported sale process starting as soon as July 2026 (Bloomberg via trade press).

productsAndServices.name: Capital-markets & securitization franchise
productsAndServices.description: A repeat-issuance funding machine second only to Vantage's in tenure: the Stack Infrastructure Issuer, LLC master trust has issued ten series of Secured Data Center Revenue Notes since 2019 (2019-1, 2019-2, 2020-1, 2021-1, 2023-1, 2023-2, 2023-3, 2024-1, 2025-1, 2026-1). The company reported $2.83B of cumulative notes through the $240M green Series 2024-1 (March 2024, its 'lowest spread over treasuries for a data center issuer since October 2021'); Series 2025-1 added $345M at 5.00% (ARD May 2030, A-(sf) by S&P, closed 22 May 2025) and Series 2026-1 added $695M at 5.0% (ARD March 2031, closed 3 March 2026, partly refinancing existing ABS) — ~$3.9B cumulative. The green-loan stack runs region by region: $900M for NVA05 (January 2025), $4B for Stafford/Portland/Toronto (March 2025), $3B for Prince William/Phoenix/Atlanta covering 900MW (August 2024), $1.3B global (June 2024), AUD $1.3B for MEL01 (July 2025, five mandated lead arrangers) and ¥39.7B for TKY01 (October 2025). Cumulative disclosures: $15B+ total funding (August 2024) → $20B of debt capital (March 2025) → $36.1B of global capital raised (July 2025). At the sponsor level, Blue Owl seeded its perpetual non-traded REIT (Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Trust) with 11 stabilized STACK-operated data centers — $3.3B gross enterprise value, $1.5B net of assumed debt, 163MW at 99.6% leased — on 1 December 2025.
highlights: Ten ABS series since 2019 under one A-(sf)-rated master trust — build, lease, securitize, recycle
Local-currency green financings (AUD, JPY) match each regional platform to its own lender base
The ODIT seeding created a permanent-capital exit lane for stabilized assets that finite-life funds previously had to sell outright
productsAndServices.positioning: Smaller cumulative program than Vantage's (which invented the asset class in 2018 and opened the sterling/euro markets) but among the sector's most consistent issuers — six-plus funding events across 2023-2026 through rate cycles; the Blue Owl relationship adds a perpetual-vehicle takeout no independent developer can replicate.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: 144A/private-placement securitized notes off the master trust; syndicated green term loans per region; sponsor equity from Blue Owl-managed digital infrastructure funds (formerly IPI funds).
targetSegments: Blue Owl perpetual-capital vehicles and their wealth-channel investors
productsAndServices.roadmap: Reported APAC portfolio sale (>$30B potential, process from ~July 2026 per Bloomberg-sourced reporting) would be the franchise's largest capital event; continued master-trust issuance implied by the 2026-1 refinancing pattern.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess STACK is the Blue Owl complex's named-tenant build engine — the only private platform holding developer-owner roles in both an Amazon state-scale program and a Stargate site. Basis: developer and owner of all three campuses in Amazon's northwest Louisiana buildout, raised from $12B to $18B in six months (Aug 2026), plus Project Jupiter (1GW+, Santa Teresa, NM) in the Oracle/OpenAI Stargate expansion — disclosed program wins larger than anything named at Aligned or QTS.

(High confidence) We assess the sponsor is running a monetize-while-building barbell: sell stabilized and regional assets at AI-era marks while the development engine compounds. Basis: the Apollo carve-out of the pan-European colocation business (Apr 2025), the perpetual non-traded REIT seeded with 11 stabilized STACK data centers at $3.3B gross value (Dec 2025), and Bloomberg-reported preparation of an APAC portfolio sale that could exceed $30B (Jun 2026) — three monetization moves in fourteen months against a stated 13GW pipeline.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Americas leadership rebuild treats power procurement and community consent as the binding constraints on delivery. Basis: Microsoft's VP of Energy (Bobby Hollis) hired as Chief Development Officer (May 2026), a hyperscaler site-selection veteran (Matt VanderZanden) installed as Americas CEO (Dec 2025), and external affairs elevated to the C-suite in the March 2026 management expansion.

(Moderate confidence) We assess regional ring-fencing is deliberate financial architecture, not an org chart: each platform carries its own currency-matched capital stack, which makes any region separately sellable. Basis: yen green financing for the Tokyo flagship (Oct 2025), AUD $1.3B for Melbourne (Jul 2025), a US master-trust ABS running ten series since 2019 (Series 2026-1, $695M) — and the fact that both the European carve-out and the reported APAC sale can execute without touching the Americas trust.

(Low confidence) We assess anchor concentration is quietly becoming STACK's version of Vantage's Stargate exposure. Basis: the Louisiana program's growth to $18B makes Amazon the platform's largest disclosed commitment, and outside ABS collateral the company publishes no tenant-diversification data. Collection gap: no revenue, EBITDA or tenant-mix disclosure anywhere in the public record.

metrics.name: Formation
metrics.actual: Created January 2019 by IPI Partners (ICONIQ Capital/Iron Point Partners JV) combining Infomart Data Centers' Ashburn, Portland and Silicon Valley facilities with IPI's Atlanta, Chicago and two Dallas/Fort Worth assets — 100MW+ across ~1.5M sq ft
metrics.result: Founding CEO Brian Cox (ex-Infomart, ex-Cologix); equity value at formation not disclosed

metrics.name: Manager change
metrics.actual: Blue Owl Capital acquired IPI Partners' business for ~$1.0B (~80% Blue Owl equity / ~20% cash) — announced 7 October 2024, completed 6 January 2025; IPI had $11B+ AUM and 82 data centers / 2.2GW at announcement; IPI managing partner Matt A'Hearn became Head of Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure
metrics.result: STACK's controlling funds became Blue Owl-managed; ICONIQ affiliate retained a services agreement

metrics.name: Perpetual-capital vehicle
metrics.actual: Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Trust (perpetual non-traded REIT, formed April 2025) raised $1.7B and on 1 December 2025 acquired 11 stabilized STACK-operated US data centers from the BODI I funds — $3.3B gross enterprise value, $1.5B net purchase price after assumed debt; 163MW, 99.6% leased
metrics.result: Stabilized STACK assets now sit partly in permanent capital, with STACK retained as operator

metrics.name: Reported APAC sale
metrics.actual: Bloomberg-sourced reports (June 2026): Blue Owl preparing a sale of STACK's APAC portfolio that could exceed $30B; AIP (BlackRock/Microsoft/MGX), Brookfield, IFM, KKR and DigitalBridge among reported suitors; process as soon as July 2026
metrics.result: Unconfirmed by the company; would be among the largest data-center transactions on record

periods.commentary: Fund-level ownership percentages across BODI/IPI vehicles are not disclosed. The chain today: Blue Owl Capital (manager) → Blue Owl-managed digital infrastructure funds and ODIT (owners) → STACK regional operating platforms.

metrics.name: Master-trust securitizations
metrics.actual: Ten series since 2019 (2019-1 through 2026-1): $2.83B cumulative through the $240M green Series 2024-1 (March 2024, 'lowest spread over treasuries for a data-center issuer since October 2021'); Series 2025-1 $345M at 5.00%, ARD May 2030, A-(sf) by S&P (May 2025); Series 2026-1 $695M at 5.0%, ARD March 2031 (March 2026, partly refinancing existing ABS) — ~$3.9B cumulative issuance
metrics.result: One of the sector's most consistent repeat issuers behind first-mover Vantage

metrics.name: Green loans (Americas)
metrics.actual: $900M for NVA05 Manassas (January 2025); $4B for Stafford 1+GW / Portland / Toronto (March 2025); $3B for Prince William, Phoenix and Atlanta campuses totaling 900MW (August 2024); $1.3B global development financing (June 2024)
metrics.result: $9B of Virginia financings since 2019; company claims the largest-private-developer position in Virginia

metrics.name: Green loans (APAC)
metrics.actual: AUD $1.3B for MEL01 West Melbourne (July 2025; Deutsche Bank, MUFG, Natixis, OCBC, SocGen MLAs) — >$2B of Australian financings since Q2 2024; ¥39.7B (~$260M) for TKY01 Inzai (October 2025)
metrics.result: Local-currency financing per platform keeps each region separately bankable — and separable

metrics.name: Cumulative capital
metrics.actual: $15B+ total funding (August 2024) → $20B of debt capital across the global portfolio (March 2025) → $36.1B of global capital raised (July 2025)
metrics.result: The company's own running counter; no later cumulative figure disclosed through August 2026

periods.commentary: Collection gap: STACK discloses no consolidated leverage, interest coverage or notes-outstanding total; the ~$3.9B securitization figure is cumulative issuance, not current outstanding (Series 2026-1 partly refinanced earlier vintages).

metrics.name: Platform
metrics.actual: 13GW of current and pipeline capacity across Americas, EMEA and APAC (company statement, December 2025); more than 90 US data centers in operation, under construction and under development (company statement, August 2026)
metrics.result: The 13GW figure mixes operational and pipeline capacity; built IT load is materially lower

metrics.name: Regional footprints
metrics.actual: Americas: 3,200MW site capacity, 23 campuses, 1,360 acres (2,400MW across 7 Northern Virginia sites). EMEA: 743MW, 21 campuses, 322 acres (Milan 399MW across 11 sites). APAC: campuses in Melbourne (432MW/2 sites), Sydney (450MW filed), Johor (216MW), Osaka (72MW), Tokyo (36MW)
metrics.result: Company website figures, August 2026; per-market numbers are buildout capacity, not leased load

metrics.name: Headcount
metrics.actual: ~900 employees globally across ~20 markets (February 2025, per Blue Owl Digital Infrastructure Trust SEC filing)
metrics.result: Latest disclosed figure; excludes the divested European colocation staff who transferred to the Apollo carve-out

periods.commentary: Collection gap: STACK publishes no revenue, EBITDA, or consolidated balance-sheet figures — it is private with no public filings of its own, and no analyst consensus exists, so every 'expected' field is left empty. A second gap: leased-versus-built capacity is never broken out, and the APAC locations page's regional total (470MW/4 campuses) conflicts with its own per-market figures — capacity claims should be treated as pipeline-inclusive. A third gap: Louisiana program megawatts are not company-disclosed; only the $18B investment, jobs and parish locations are on the record (third-party trackers cite ~3GW, unverified).

financials.commentary: Collection gap: STACK has never disclosed revenue, EBITDA, leverage or tenant-mix figures — the platform's scale must be read from capacity statements (13GW current + pipeline, Dec 2025), cumulative-capital disclosures ($36.1B through Jul 2025), securitization collateral data and sponsor (Blue Owl) reporting. Valuation marks for the reported APAC sale (>$30B) and the REIT seed ($3.3B gross, 11 assets) are press- and sponsor-attributed respectively. No analyst consensus exists for any period — every 'expected' field is left empty rather than reconstructed.
